classification.difficultyReason: Substitute the complete rational expression into both occurrences of the function input, clear the internal denominator and simplify parameter expressions to expose a cancellable non-zero factor. The composition and required restrictions are supplied.

content.prompt:
[Self-inverse functions]

Let $a$ and $b$ be non-zero real numbers with $ab\ne-1$, and define the function $$f(x)=\frac{a-x}{1+bx}.$$ Show that $$f\left(\frac{a-x}{1+bx}\right)=x,$$ where $x\ne-\dfrac1b$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}f\left(\frac{a-x}{1+bx}\right)&=\frac{a-\frac{a-x}{1+bx}}{1+b\frac{a-x}{1+bx}}\\f\left(\frac{a-x}{1+bx}\right)&=\frac{a(1+bx)-(a-x)}{1+bx+b(a-x)}\\f\left(\frac{a-x}{1+bx}\right)&=\frac{abx+x}{1+ab}\\f\left(\frac{a-x}{1+bx}\right)&=\frac{x(ab+1)}{ab+1}\\f\left(\frac{a-x}{1+bx}\right)&=x.\end{align*}$$
The denominators are non-zero because $x\ne-\dfrac1b$ and $ab\ne-1$.
